title: Inner Join Matched Sales
description:
Finance only wants overnight sales that exist in the merchandising catalog. Orphan SKUs (new ids not yet in products) should be dropped — not kept with a null name.

**Inner-join** sales (`INPUT_PATH`) to products (`PRODUCTS_PATH`) on `product_id` and add `product_name`. Keep only sales rows that match the catalog. Write Parquet with overwrite.

Sales columns: `txn_id`, `product_id`, `store_id`, `quantity`. Products columns: `product_id` (unique), `product_name`. Output: all sales columns plus `product_name`. Use an explicit inner join (`how="inner"`) — a left join would keep orphans with null names. Implement with Spark DataFrame APIs — no driver-side nested loops over `collect`. **Run** uses two smoke testcases; **Submit** uses the full set and row-diffs your Parquet against each case’s `expected/`.

Write results with `df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(OUTPUT_PATH)`. `OUTPUT_PATH` is set by the platform for **this Run/Submit only**.

problemStatement.overview: Inner-join sales to products on product_id; keep only matched sales with product_name; write Parquet to OUTPUT_PATH.
symptoms: Finance totals include orphan SKUs that are not in the catalog yet.
A left join would keep those orphans with null product_name — this lab must drop them.
yourTaskSteps: Read sales from INPUT_PATH and products from PRODUCTS_PATH.
Inner-join on product_id and add product_name (unmatched sales are dropped).
Write txn_id, product_id, store_id, quantity, product_name to OUTPUT_PATH with overwrite.
Submit is graded with a row-level compare against each selected testcase expected/.
problemStatement.yourTask: Implement src/main.py that inner-joins sales to the product catalog.
hints: A left join would keep orphan sales with product_name null — that fails this lab.
Product keys are unique — one output row per matched sales row.
broadcast(products) is allowed but not required.

expectedOutput.description: Sales line id (grade key); orphans omitted
From products via inner join (non-null for kept rows)
